Content:
In previous lessons, we explored how to convert larger metric units of length to smaller ones. In this lesson, we will learn how to convert smaller metric units of length to larger ones.

Content:
To convert between metric units of length, we use the following unit conversions:

Content:
- [MATH: 1] centimeter [MATH: = 10] millimeters
- [MATH: 1] meter [MATH: =100] centimeters
- [MATH: 1] kilometer [MATH: =1,000] meters

Content:
We can visualize equivalent units of length using measuring instruments. For example, the meterstick below shows the equivalence between [MATH: 1] meter and [MATH: 100] centimeters.

Graphic:

Let's get some practice at converting between different units of length.

items.readable_text:
Content:
Suppose we want to convert [MATH: 420] millimeters to centimeters. We start with the unit conversion between centimeters and millimeters:

Content:
[MATH: 1 \,\textrm{cm} = 10 \,\textrm{mm}]

Content:
Since we are converting from millimeters to centimeters, we divide both sides of the above equation by [MATH: 10] and obtain the following:

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{1}{10} \,\textrm{cm} = 1 \,\textrm{mm}]

Content:
The right-hand side reads [MATH: 1\,\textrm{mm},] and we want to know how many centimeters are in [MATH: \color{blue}420] millimeters. So, we multiply both sides of this equation by [MATH: {\color{blue}{420}}.]

Content:
[MATH: 420 × (1)/(10)cm|= 420 × 1mm; (420 ÷ 10)cm|= 420mm; 42cm|= 420mm]

Content:
Therefore, [MATH: 420] millimeters equals [MATH: 42] centimeters.

sections.normalized_html: What is [MATH: 14\,\textrm{mm}] in centimeters?
sections.readable_text: What is [MATH: 14\,\textrm{mm}] in centimeters?

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
We need to convert [MATH: 14] millimeters to centimeters.

We start with the unit conversion between centimeters and millimeters:

[MATH: 1 \,\textrm{cm} = 10 \,\textrm{mm}]

Since we are converting from millimeters to centimeters, we divide both sides of the above equation by [MATH: 10] and obtain the following:

[MATH: \dfrac{1}{10} \,\textrm{cm} = 1 \,\textrm{mm}]

We want to determine how many centimeters are in [MATH: 14] millimeters. So, we multiply both sides of the above equation by [MATH: 14{:}]

[MATH: 14 × (1)/(10)cm|= 14 × 1mm; (14 ÷ 10)cm|= 14mm; 1.4cm|= 14mm]

Therefore, [MATH: 14\,\textrm{mm}] equals [MATH: 1.4\,\textrm{cm}.]

Since we are converting from centimeters to meters, we divide both sides of the above equation by [MATH: 100] and obtain the following:

[MATH: \dfrac{1}{100} \,\textrm{m} = 1 \,\textrm{cm}]

Therefore, [MATH: 363\,\textrm{cm}] equals [MATH: 3.63\,\textrm{m}.]
